name: Mordell Conjecture (Faltings's Theorem)
description: A smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus greater than 1 over a number field has only finitely many rational points.
source_article: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Chabauty's Method
description: A p-adic technique that, when the Mordell-Weil rank of the Jacobian is less than the genus, cuts out the rational points of a curve as the common zeros of certain p-adic abelian integrals on the p-adic points lying in the closure of the Mordell-Weil group.
source_article: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Coleman's Effective Chabauty Bound
description: Under the Chabauty rank hypothesis, the number of rational points of a curve of genus g with good reduction at a prime p greater than 2g is at most the number of points modulo p plus 2g minus 2.
source_article: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Kim's Nonabelian Chabauty Method
description: A generalization of Chabauty's method replacing the Jacobian by the unipotent (de Rham/etale) fundamental group, locating rational points inside a Selmer-type p-adic locus cut out by iterated Coleman integrals.
source_article: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Quadratic Chabauty
description: The depth-two explicit instance of Kim's method (Balakrishnan-Dogra) that uses p-adic height pairings to produce an explicit finite locus containing the rational points when the rank equals the genus.
source_article: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Lawrence-Venkatesh Method
description: A proof of the Mordell conjecture using a Kodaira-Parshin family of covers and p-adic Hodge theory to show that the p-adic Galois representations attached to fibers vary so much that only finitely many fibers can sit over rational points.
source_article: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Skolem's Method
description: A p-adic method for integral points that expresses solutions as zeros of p-adic analytic functions whose finiteness follows from the Strassmann/Weierstrass preparation property of convergent p-adic power series.
source_article: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Cap Set Problem
description: The problem of bounding the maximal size of a subset of the affine space F_3^n containing no three collinear points (no nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression).
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Croot-Lev-Pach-Ellenberg-Gijswijt Theorem
description: Every cap set in F_3^n has size at most a constant times 2.756^n, an exponential improvement over the trivial 3^n obtained via the polynomial method.
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Polynomial Method (combinatorics)
description: A proof strategy in which a low-degree polynomial vanishing on a combinatorial configuration is constructed and its algebraic properties (degree, zero set, rank) are used to bound the size of the configuration.
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Slice Rank Method
description: Tao's reformulation of the cap set argument via the slice rank of a tensor, defined as the minimal number of summands each factoring through a single variable, which is submultiplicative and bounds the diagonal of a tensor.
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Analytic L-function (axiomatic)
description: A Dirichlet series with Euler product, meromorphic continuation, and a functional equation relating s to 1-s, packaged with prescribed analytic data such as conductor, gamma factors, and central character.
source_article: Analytic L-functions: definitions, theorems, and connections, Farmer, Pitale, Ryan, and Schmidt, 2019

name: Selberg Class
description: The class of Dirichlet series satisfying Selberg's axioms (Ramanujan bound, analytic continuation, functional equation, and Euler product), conjecturally coinciding with automorphic L-functions.
source_article: Analytic L-functions: definitions, theorems, and connections, Farmer, Pitale, Ryan, and Schmidt, 2019

name: Analytic Conductor
description: A real-valued invariant of an L-function combining its arithmetic conductor with the spectral parameters of its gamma factors, governing the density of zeros and the analytic complexity of the function.
source_article: Analytic L-functions: definitions, theorems, and connections, Farmer, Pitale, Ryan, and Schmidt, 2019

name: Algebraic Hypersurface
description: The zero locus in projective space of a single homogeneous polynomial, regarded as a degree-d divisor whose geometry depends sharply on d relative to the ambient dimension.
source_article: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Rational Variety
description: A variety that is birationally equivalent to projective space, i.e. admits a parametrization by independent rational functions invertible on a dense open set.
source_article: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Unirational Variety
description: A variety that admits a dominant rational map from projective space, i.e. can be rationally parametrized but not necessarily birationally.
source_article: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Stably Rational Variety
description: A variety X such that X times some projective space is rational, an intermediate notion strictly between rational and unirational.
source_article: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Luroth Problem
description: The question of whether every unirational variety is rational, answered affirmatively for curves and surfaces but negatively in dimension three and higher.
source_article: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Decomposition of the Diagonal Method
description: An obstruction to (stable) rationality showing that a stably rational variety admits a Chow-theoretic decomposition of its diagonal, whose failure under specialization (Voisin, Colliot-Thelene-Pirutka) certifies non-stable-rationality.
source_article: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Non-Stable-Rationality of Very General Hypersurfaces
description: A very general hypersurface of sufficiently high degree in projective space (degree at least roughly two-thirds the dimension, after Totaro and Schreieder) is not stably rational.
source_article: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Stable Rationality of Cubic Hypersurfaces (low degree)
description: Smooth cubic and other low-degree hypersurfaces are unirational, and rationality holds in classical small cases, illustrating the boundary between rational and irrational hypersurfaces.
source_article: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Big Polynomial Ring / Uniformity (Erman-Sam-Snowden)
description: The phenomenon, formalized via the inverse-limit polynomial ring in infinitely many variables and GL-equivariant commutative algebra, that bounds on invariants of cubic (and higher-degree) forms become independent of the number of variables.
source_article: Cubics in 10 variables vs. cubics in 1000 variables: uniformity phenomena, Erman, Sam, and Snowden, 2019

name: Stillman's Conjecture (Theorem)
description: The projective dimension of an ideal generated by a fixed number of homogeneous polynomials of fixed degrees is bounded independently of the number of variables of the ambient polynomial ring.
source_article: Cubics in 10 variables vs. cubics in 1000 variables: uniformity phenomena, Erman, Sam, and Snowden, 2019

name: Strength of a Polynomial
description: The least number r such that a homogeneous form is a sum of r products of lower-degree forms, a measure of degeneracy that controls uniform algebraic behavior of higher-degree forms.
source_article: Cubics in 10 variables vs. cubics in 1000 variables: uniformity phenomena, Erman, Sam, and Snowden, 2019

name: Tangent Developable Surface
description: The surface swept out by the tangent lines to a space curve, a ruled surface naturally attached to the curve whose singular structure encodes the curve's projective geometry.
source_article: Tangent developable surfaces and the equations defining algebraic curves, Ein and Lazarsfeld, 2020

name: Green's Conjecture
description: The Clifford index of a smooth projective curve equals the index of the first nonzero linear syzygy in the minimal free resolution of its canonical embedding, proved generically by Voisin and in general using degenerations to tangent developable surfaces.
source_article: Tangent developable surfaces and the equations defining algebraic curves, Ein and Lazarsfeld, 2020

name: Koszul Cohomology / Property N_p
description: The graded groups computing the syzygies of an embedded variety, with property N_p meaning the resolution is linear up to homological degree p, governing how a curve is cut out by quadrics and higher relations.
source_article: Tangent developable surfaces and the equations defining algebraic curves, Ein and Lazarsfeld, 2020

name: Degeneration to Tangent Developable Surfaces (technique)
description: A proof method computing syzygies of canonical curves by specializing to the tangent developable of a rational normal curve and using its explicit, computable resolution.
source_article: Tangent developable surfaces and the equations defining algebraic curves, Ein and Lazarsfeld, 2020

name: Moduli Space (axiomatic)
description: A space whose points parametrize isomorphism classes of geometric objects (curves, abelian varieties, sheaves) with a universal family encoding their variation.
source_article: Compactifying moduli spaces, Lucia Caporaso, 2020

name: Deligne-Mumford Compactification of M_g
description: The compactification of the moduli space of smooth genus-g curves by adjoining stable nodal curves, yielding a projective Deligne-Mumford stack.
source_article: Compactifying moduli spaces, Lucia Caporaso, 2020

name: Stable Curve
description: A connected nodal projective curve of arithmetic genus g whose only singularities are nodes and whose automorphism group is finite (equivalently, every rational component meets the rest in at least three points).
source_article: Compactifying moduli spaces, Lucia Caporaso, 2020

name: Compactified Jacobian / Universal Picard Variety
description: A compactification of the moduli of line bundles over a family of curves, including degenerate nodal fibers, parametrizing rank-one torsion-free sheaves with a stability condition.
source_article: Compactifying moduli spaces, Lucia Caporaso, 2020

name: Tropical / Dual-Graph Combinatorics of the Boundary
description: The encoding of the boundary strata of compactified moduli spaces by the dual graphs of stable curves, linking the geometry to tropical moduli and combinatorial polyhedral data.
source_article: Compactifying moduli spaces, Lucia Caporaso, 2020

name: Space of Diagonal Harmonics
description: The bigraded vector space DH_n of polynomials in two sets of n variables killed by all symmetric-group-invariant differential operators with positive degree, carrying a diagonal S_n-action.
source_article: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Nabla Operator
description: The Garsia-Bergeron linear operator on symmetric functions that is diagonal in the modified Macdonald polynomial basis with explicit eigenvalues, whose value on the elementary symmetric function e_n equals the bigraded Frobenius characteristic of diagonal harmonics.
source_article: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Parking Function (combinatorics)
description: A Dyck path of order n together with a column-increasing labeling of its north steps by 1,...,n, equipped with the statistics area and dinv (diagonal inversions).
source_article: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Shuffle Conjecture (Theorem)
description: The symmetric function nabla(e_n) equals the weighted generating function over parking functions of order n with weight q to the dinv, t to the area, times the quasisymmetric function of the function's descent set.
source_article: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Compositional Shuffle Conjecture (Theorem)
description: A refinement of the shuffle conjecture indexed by compositions, controlling the touch points of the Dyck path, whose proof by Carlsson and Mellit (via the Dyck path / double affine Hecke algebra) implies the shuffle conjecture.
source_article: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Overconvergent Modular Form
description: A p-adic modular form that converges on a strict neighborhood of the ordinary locus of the modular curve, organized into Coleman's finite-slope eigenvariety theory.
source_article: Overconvergent modular forms and their explicit arithmetic, Jan Vonk, 2021

name: U_p Operator and Slope Decomposition
description: The completely continuous Atkin-Lehner operator on spaces of overconvergent forms whose generalized eigenspaces of finite slope (p-adic valuation of eigenvalue) give the finite-slope classical and overconvergent forms.
source_article: Overconvergent modular forms and their explicit arithmetic, Jan Vonk, 2021

name: Coleman Classicality Theorem
description: An overconvergent eigenform of weight k and slope strictly less than k minus 1 is a classical modular form.
source_article: Overconvergent modular forms and their explicit arithmetic, Jan Vonk, 2021

name: Rigid Meromorphic Cocycles / p-adic Singular Moduli
description: The Darmon-Vonk p-adic analogues of singular moduli, constructed from overconvergent forms and real quadratic geodesics, conjecturally algebraic and refining the theory of complex multiplication to real quadratic fields.
source_article: Overconvergent modular forms and their explicit arithmetic, Jan Vonk, 2021

name: Classical Siegel-Weil Formula
description: An identity expressing a special value of a Siegel Eisenstein series as the average over a genus of theta series of quadratic forms, equating an Eisenstein series with an integral of theta functions.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Special Cycles on Shimura Varieties
description: Algebraic cycles on orthogonal or unitary Shimura varieties indexed by positive-definite quadratic/Hermitian data, generalizing Heegner points to higher codimension.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Kudla's Modularity Conjecture (Theorem)
description: The generating series whose coefficients are the classes of special cycles of a fixed codimension in the Chow group of a Shimura variety is a (vector-valued) modular form.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Geometric Siegel-Weil Formula
description: An identity expressing the special value of a Siegel Eisenstein series as a generating series of degrees/volumes of special cycles on a Shimura variety, lifting the classical formula to geometry.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil Formula
description: An identity relating arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on integral models of Shimura varieties to derivatives of Siegel Eisenstein series at the near-central point.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Kudla-Rapoport Conjecture (Theorem)
description: A local identity equating the arithmetic intersection number of special cycles on a Rapoport-Zink space with the derivative of a local representation/Whittaker density, proved by Li and Zhang.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Rapoport-Zink Space
description: A formal/rigid moduli space of p-divisible groups with additional structure (polarization, level), serving as the local p-adic uniformization of Shimura varieties.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Arithmetic Inner Product Formula
description: An identity relating the Beilinson-Bloch height of an arithmetic theta lift cycle to the central derivative of an L-function, generalizing the Gross-Zagier formula to higher dimension.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Beilinson-Bloch Conjecture
description: The conjecture that the rank of the Chow group of homologically trivial cycles on a smooth projective variety equals the order of vanishing of the associated L-function at the central point.
source_article: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Gorenstein Ring
description: A Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension over itself, equivalently a Cohen-Macaulay ring whose canonical module is free of rank one, with a symmetric free resolution.
source_article: F. S. Macaulay: from plane curves to Gorenstein rings, Eisenbud and Gray, 2023

name: Macaulay Inverse System
description: A duality, due to Macaulay, between Artinian quotients of a polynomial ring and finitely generated submodules of the dual divided-power (or polynomial) module under contraction, parametrizing such quotients by inverse systems.
source_article: F. S. Macaulay: from plane curves to Gorenstein rings, Eisenbud and Gray, 2023

name: Unmixedness / Macaulay's Theorem on Complete Intersections
description: An ideal generated by n elements in a polynomial ring whose codimension equals n is unmixed (all associated primes have the same codimension), an early structural result foreshadowing Cohen-Macaulay theory.
source_article: F. S. Macaulay: from plane curves to Gorenstein rings, Eisenbud and Gray, 2023

name: Embedding Q into a Finitely Presented Group (Theorem)
description: The additive group of rational numbers embeds into a finitely presented group, realized via Belk-Hyde-Matucci using twisted Brin-Thompson groups acting on Cantor space.
source_article: Embedding Q into a finitely presented group, Belk, Hyde, and Matucci, 2022

name: Twisted Brin-Thompson Group
description: A group of homeomorphisms of a Cantor space built from a base group acting on an alphabet together with prefix-replacement (Thompson-type) moves, simple and finitely presented under mild hypotheses.
source_article: Embedding Q into a finitely presented group, Belk, Hyde, and Matucci, 2022
